newsitem.title: USA: PSA backs Senate finance panel tax package.
newsitem.headline: PSA backs Senate finance panel tax package.

text.p: PSA The Bond Market Trade Association said Friday it backs the tax legislation approved by the Senate Finance Committee late Thursday.

"PSA supports the bill because it represents a balanced approach to balancing the federal budget, providing necessary tax relief without increasing the cost of capital for states, localities and corporations," Micah Green, PSA executive vice president, said in a telephone interview.
Green said his group is particularly pleased that the bill would not repeal the so-called de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of municipal bonds.
A bill cleared by the House Ways and Means Committee last week would scale back the de minimis exemption for corporate holdings of munis to a flat $1 million.
Muni lobbyists said the House panel bill would virtually gut the provision's usefulness for the market.

PSA also is pleased that the Senate committee measure does not include a controversial proposal by Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, D-N.Y., to bar the use of tax-exempt bonds for construction of professional sports stadiums, Green said.
Another Moynihan idea that does appear in the Senate committee bill - but that does has PSA's blessing - would repeal the current $150 million limit on 501(c)(3) bond volume.

So-called 501(c)(3) bonds are issued by not-for-profit organizations other than hospitals, such as universities, nursing homes and museums. The federal government currently "caps" the total volume of such bonds that localities can issue at $150 million.
Ways and Means last week approved a more modest expansion of the volume cap to $200 million over five years.
Senate finance panel aides said they expect the committee's tax package to reach the Senate floor for a vote by June 27.
